summary: With Quick Look open in its own window, GPUI could hand the browser's field handlers Quick Look's window, or no window at all. `Context::subscribe_in` and `observe_in` don't keep the window they are given: when the event comes they ask for the last window that read the subscriber while drawing a frame (`current_window_by_entity`, written at the end of every `Window::draw`), and Quick Look's window reads its browser to draw the preview. The browser now subscribes through two small helpers in src/finder/mod.rs, `Finder::subscribe_in_window` and `Finder::observe_in_window`. They subscribe at the App level and run the handler through the browser's own window handle, taken when subscribing, so it still runs once, at the same point of the effect flush, and always in the browser's window. They are used for the search field, the filter field, the Nushell field and the shared settings (Finder::new), for a name being edited in place (src/finder/inline_rename.rs) and for the field of the dialog that renames several items (src/finder/batch_rename.rs).
changelog: With Quick Look open, Return in the search field sometimes selected the first result but left the keyboard in the search field, and Quick Look then ignored Escape, Space, and the arrow keys until it was clicked. Pressed before the results were in, Return did nothing. Return after editing a name in place could leave the arrow keys and the other file keys doing nothing until a click. All of it happened when Quick Look's window was the last of the two to redraw before the key. Return now acts in the window it was pressed in.
behaviour_changes: Everything here needs Quick Look open in its own window. For 1 to 4 its window also has to be the last of the two to have drawn when the key arrives, with no mouse event in the browser's window since the key before (GPUI redraws a window before the first key after the mouse). Typing and then pressing Return is that case.

1. Return in the search field with the results in: the browser's files get the keyboard and the first result is selected. Before: the first result was selected, the keyboard stayed in the search field, and Quick Look's window was given the files' focus. I saw the rest on the unfixed build: Right, Space and Escape in Quick Look then did nothing, and after a click on its caption Right moved the selection and Escape closed it.

2. Return in the search field before the results are in: the key waits and the keyboard moves into the results when they arrive, also if Quick Look is closed in the meantime. Before: nothing happened when they arrived.

3. Return in a name being edited in place: the item is renamed and the keyboard goes back to the files, or to the sidebar's tree when the name was edited there. Before: the item was renamed, the field was removed, and the browser's keyboard stayed on it. On the unfixed build, in the list view, Down, a typed letter and Cmd+A then did nothing until a click on a row. On the fixed build I also tried the icon view and the sidebar's tree.

4. The same Return in a window with tabs, in split view's first pane and in a file chooser (--pick): wrong on the unfixed build, right on the fixed one. The split pane Quick Look doesn't belong to was right on both.

5. When Quick Look's window was the last to draw a browser and then closes, GPUI has no window on record for that browser until the browser's own window draws again, and it skipped every one of these handlers meanwhile. They now run. Seen on the unfixed build, with the step put in the same update as the close: a favorite added in another tab did not show in the tab whose Quick Look had closed (now a test), and a letter typed in the search field was not searched for. In a window that is being drawn the gap is one frame. gpui-pre's macOS code stops drawing a window that is covered, minimized or on another Space, and there it lasts until the window shows again; that part I read and could not run.

Unchanged: everything while Quick Look is closed, in --term mode (one window), or when the browser's window drew last. Down Arrow in the search field, which is a key listener and gets the window the key was pressed in. What a field does when it loses the keyboard: a blur is reported from the browser's own frame, so its handler always had the browser's window. The filter field, the Nushell field and the batch rename dialog's field don't use the window they are handed, and the settings only ask it whether the system is light or dark; apart from 5 they do what they did.
left_out: `WeakEntity::update_in` looks its window up the same way and is untouched. See Found, not fixed in the notes: it is worth a brief of its own.

`enter_awaited_results` (mod.rs) and `QuickLookWindow::with_finder` (quick_look.rs) do the same window-then-browser update as the new private `Finder::update_in_window`. They are not folded into it, to keep to what the brief asks. `enter_results` still stores a window handle; it is now always the browser's.
src/finder/quick_look.rs, which the brief lists, is unchanged: nothing there asks GPUI for the browser's window.

No test that the filter field's, the Nushell field's and the batch rename field's handlers get the browser's window: they don't use it, so nothing a test can see differs. Existing tests cover that they still fire (the implementer silenced the three handlers in Finder::new and six filter tests, nushell_panel_controls and two settings tests failed). Putting one of those three lines back to `cx.subscribe_in` fails no test; what it would lose is item 5 of the behaviour changes for that field.
No test of the sidebar tree's rename field or of the icon and column views: they share the list view's subscription. I tried the tree and the icon view by hand on the fixed build.

No documentation change. docs/manual.md describes what Return does in the search field and in a name being edited, and nothing in it became wrong or incomplete. CHANGELOG.md is not edited, per the guide; the entry is in the commit message and in this record.
`cargo clippy --features term` was not run: src/term is untouched and no signature it calls changed. macOS and Windows were not compiled here; the change has no platform-specific code and no cfg.
No before and after pictures. Nothing is drawn differently, and shot.sh's key step draws the browser's window before the key, which hides the fault.

notes:
Checked. With the src diff reverse-applied on the trunk commit the five new tests fail, each at an assertion about the app and none at the helpers' own checks (tests/finder.rs:568, 593 and 613, tests/basics.rs:856, tests/settings.rs:116); applied again they pass, and git status was clean. With only the settings line put back to `cx.observe_in`, a_setting_reaches_a_tab_whose_quick_look_has_just_closed fails and the other thirteen tests of tests/settings.rs pass. The five pass with SEED=0, 1, 7, 42 and 1234. check.sh printed CHECK OK on the trunk commit: 579 passed in 16 test binaries, 3 of 3 known root-only failures. `cargo build --lib -p fffinder`, the library as it ships without test-support, has no warnings.

The implementer's two calls beyond the brief stand. The handlers are not re-dispatched from inside, as the brief proposed; the subscriptions are replaced, which leaves one path, nothing deferred and no handler that can run twice. And the fix covers a name being edited in place, which had the same fault and has a test, and the batch rename dialog's field, where nothing visible changes.

The cause, read in gpui-pre-0.3.10, is as the implementer has it. `Window::draw` ends with `record_entities_accessed`, which makes the drawing window the current one of every entity read in that frame (src/app.rs, `current_window_by_entity`). `subscribe_in`, `observe_in`, `defer_in` and `WeakEntity::update_in` all get their window from `App::with_window`, which reads that map, and a window that closes takes its entries with it (the tail of `update_window_erased`). Events are delivered only from `flush_effects`, which runs when no update is under way, so a handler never finds its window taken: `window.update` in the new helpers fails only when the window is gone. gpui-pre's own `Window::subscribe` and `Window::observe` keep their window the same way; they drop the subscription when the window is gone, where the helpers keep it until the browser drops it, which makes no difference here.

Throwaway probes, not kept, each run on the unfixed and on the fixed build: the Return scenario in a window with tabs, in both panes of split view and in a file chooser; Quick Look's keys after the wrong Return, and after a click in it; the keys of the files after a rename's Return; a letter typed, and a favorite added in another tab, in the same update as Quick Look's window closes; the note after Cmd+Z with Quick Look's window drawn last (see Found, not fixed). On the fixed build only: Return ending a rename in the icon view and in the sidebar's tree.

The picture is the browser after Return in the search field with Quick Look open, by the ordinary path (shot.sh's key step): the first result has the selection colour the files show when they have the keyboard. It shows nothing new; nothing is drawn differently by this change.

The three ways I thought this most likely to hurt a user, and what the code says.
(1) A field stops answering at all: typing doesn't search, Return doesn't rename, another tab's setting doesn't arrive. That would take a subscription holding a window that isn't the browser's, or `window.update` failing when the event comes. Each of the three places that subscribe takes the window its caller was handed, and I followed the callers: Finder::new from the window's own build closure, new_tab and toggle_split (workspace.rs, new_finder); start_rename_field from the Rename and New Folder actions and the sidebar tree's menu; open_batch_rename from the Rename action. None is reached through `update_in`, which is what could hand over Quick Look's window. A browser never moves to another window: Move Tab to New Window builds a new one. Events arrive with every window off the update stack. And the whole suite passes, which drives these handlers in hundreds of tests.
(2) A handler now runs in another window than before, or runs where it was skipped, and does harm there. A handler that ran in Quick Look's window now runs in the browser's, where it runs whenever Quick Look is closed; none of the fields is ever drawn in Quick Look's window, so none can want it. `rename_field_blurred` asks whether its window is active, but a blur is reported from the browser's own frame (Window::draw calls the focus listeners before it records what the frame read, and the event is delivered after), so it always had the browser's window. `adopt_settings` hands the window only to `theme::apply`, which reads the system appearance from it. A handler that was skipped for want of a window now runs: the key or the setting is acted on, which is what was asked for.
(3) A panic or a leak on the way out: a window closing with an event on its way, a tab closing during a rename, the rename's subscription dropped from inside its own handler (finish_rename takes `self.renaming`). The closure holds the browser weakly and the window by handle and gives up when either is gone; the Subscription is owned by the browser or by the rename, as before; `App::subscribe` keeps it in the same set `subscribe_in` did, which puts off a removal made during a call. Tried: Quick Look closed during the wait (a test), closed in the same update as a key and as a setting (probe and test), and Return ending a rename (test).

Doubts that remain.
1. Only Linux was built and run. How often a Mac hits the fault I can only read: gpui-pre-macos stops a window's display link while the window is covered, minimized or on another Space (src/window.rs, window_did_change_occlusion_state). Quick Look opens centered over the browser at 80% of its width and 85% of its height, so once the browser is clicked to type in it, Quick Look's window is behind it and no longer drawn, and the fault can't happen. On a Mac it needs Quick Look's window where it still shows: moved beside the browser, sticking out from behind it, or on another display. I did not establish whether Linux and Windows go on drawing a covered window; if they do, the fault is the ordinary case there.
2. Three of the six subscriptions (filter field, Nushell field, batch rename field) are covered only by tests that they fire, see left_out.

For briefs still to come.
- Every brief that gives the browser a new text field or another entity to listen to: use `Self::subscribe_in_window(&entity, window, cx, handler)` or `Self::observe_in_window(..)` where the handler takes a window, or plain `cx.subscribe` / `cx.observe` where it doesn't. `cx.subscribe_in`, `cx.observe_in`, `cx.defer_in` and `this.update_in` hand a browser's handler the window that last drew the browser, which can be Quick Look's, and skip the handler when that window has closed and the browser's hasn't drawn since. `subscribe_in_window` is `pub(super)`, so the other files of src/finder can call it; the window it is given must be the browser's own, as it is in any action or element listener of the browser.
- focus-lost-recovery: your plan adds `cx.on_focus_lost(window, ..)` with `cx.defer_in(window, |_, window, _| window.refresh())` to the `subscriptions` vec in Finder::new, where four lines now read `Self::subscribe_in_window(..)` and `Self::observe_in_window(..)`; expect a small textual conflict. `on_focus_lost` is kept by the window itself and is right. `defer_in` uses the lookup. It resolves to the browser's window there, because the listener runs inside the browser's own frame, but `window.defer(cx, |window, _| window.refresh())` keeps the window and doesn't depend on that.
- choose-nu-path: your plan says `cx.spawn_in(window, ..)` and `this.update_in`. `set_nu_path(path, cx)` needs no window, so use `this.update(cx, ..)`: `update_in` is skipped altogether when GPUI has no window on record for the browser, and gets Quick Look's window when that drew last. Where a task does need the window, `cx.update(|window, cx| this.update(cx, |this, cx| ..))` uses the task's own.
- get-info-stop-walk: the two `update_in` calls you edit in src/finder/info.rs are among the twelve under Found, not fixed. With Quick Look's window drawn last, their `window.refresh()` and `window.close_dialog(cx)` go to Quick Look's window, so the panel in the browser's isn't redrawn with its sizes. If you rewrite them anyway, the form above is the one that keeps the window.
- files-changed-off-thread: src/finder/trash.rs has three of those `update_in` calls; the same applies to any you touch or add.
- smart-folder-save-and-leaks, recent-searches, live-search-results, back-forward-restore-search: `on_search_event`'s window is now always the browser's own, so it can be used there (say, to set another field's text). Its subscription line in Finder::new changed, the function itself did not.
- restore-session-tabs, tab-drop-and-close: a browser's subscriptions keep the window it was made in. A tab that goes to another window has to stay a new browser there, as `Workspace::move_tab_to_new_window` makes it, or subscribe again.
- The lanes at work now (live-search-results, back-forward-restore-search, menu-bar-mac-keys, scoped-search-special-folder-names, table-preview-scroll) and whoever rebases next: this commit added, in src/finder/mod.rs, four changed lines in the `subscriptions` vec of Finder::new and three functions right after `new`; tests after results_that_come_in_leave_the_keyboard_where_it_has_gone_since (tests/finder.rs), after moving_to_the_search_field_during_a_rename_leaves_the_keyboard_there (tests/basics.rs) and after shared_settings_show_in_every_tab_at_once (tests/settings.rs); and two helpers after `close_quick_look` in tests/common/mod.rs.
- quick-look-empty-state: src/finder/quick_look.rs is unchanged, and so is how Quick Look's window follows its browser (the observer in QuickLookWindow::new). For tests, `ui.press_after_quick_look_draws("enter")` presses a key in the browser when Quick Look's window drew last, and `ui.close_quick_look_and_then(|cx| ..)` closes Quick Look and runs a step before the browser's window draws again; both are after `close_quick_look` in tests/common/mod.rs and fail when their staging doesn't hold. The first has to follow another key, and sends no text.

Found, not fixed (on the trunk before this change, outside this brief, and worth a brief of its own): `WeakEntity::update_in` gets its window from the same lookup, even inside `cx.spawn_in(window, ..)`. Twelve calls have the browser as the entity: src/finder/trash.rs (trash_now, run_file_job, the undo and redo step), info.rs (two), volumes.rs (eject, connect), open_with.rs (after the app is chosen), transfer.rs (a spring-loaded folder, the end of a copy or move, run_job) and open_in_terminal in mod.rs. Two things go wrong.
(a) With Quick Look's window the last to draw, what the job does in a window happens in Quick Look's. Tried on both builds: after Cmd+Z, with Quick Look's window drawn before the undo finishes, the note that says what was undone is in Quick Look's window (the browser's notes 0, Quick Look's 1). Read, not tried: the notes after a trash, a copy, an eject or a failed job; `navigate`, which sets Quick Look's title instead of the browser's; Get Info's `window.refresh()` and `window.close_dialog(cx)`.
(b) With no window on record (Quick Look's window closed while it was the last to draw, and the browser's not drawn since, as when it is covered or minimized on a Mac), `update_in` returns an error, every one of these calls ends in `.ok()`, and what the job does when it finishes is dropped: for a copy or a move, its progress row is never removed, the files aren't reloaded and Undo isn't told. Read, not tried.
The fix is small at each call: `cx.update(|window, cx| this.update(cx, |this, cx| ..))` uses the task's own window, as `report_app_error` in open_with.rs already does. It is twelve calls in six files with tests of their own, several of them in files other briefs are about to change (files-changed-off-thread, get-info-stop-walk), which is why it isn't in this commit.

Scratch files: my folder lane-g-quick-look-window-mixup in the session scratchpad is deleted. The probes were temporary tests in tests/finder.rs and tests/settings.rs, removed before the commit.
